/guides/dmards-vs-biologics.answer: Biologics are a type of disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drug (DMARD). This guide compares conventional DMARDs, such as methotrexate, with biological DMARDs for inflammatory arthritis. JAK inhibitors are a separate group called targeted synthetic DMARDs, not biologics. Conventional DMARDs can help rheumatoid arthritis and peripheral joint disease, but are not recommended for purely axial spondyloarthritis affecting the spine.

faqs.a: No. JAK inhibitors are targeted synthetic DMARDs. Biological DMARDs are given by injection or infusion.

faqs.q: Do conventional DMARDs treat axial spinal disease?
faqs.a: Conventional DMARDs are not recommended for purely axial spondyloarthritis. They may help peripheral arthritis affecting other joints.
